explanation: Brazil has no cultural taboo around feet being 'unclean,' unlike Thailand or parts of the Middle East. Propping your feet up, sitting cross-legged, or letting your shoe sole show is simply informal body language — fine among friends, but better avoided in a business meeting or someone's home out of general politeness rather than any specific foot-related offense.
local_tip: Don't worry about where your soles point; just keep your feet off furniture and tables in formal settings as ordinary good manners.

also_check.note: The feet are considered the lowest, most impure part of the body; pointing them at people or sacred objects is a serious offense.
Showing the sole of your foot or shoe is a real insult, associated with dirt and disrespect.
Putting feet on furniture is generally just seen as informal or impolite in formal settings, not deeply offensive.

sources.title: Brazilian Culture - Etiquette, The Cultural Atlas
